classification.difficultyReason: Follow the supplied perpendicular construction and base-bisection fact, halve the base, and use inverse cosine in the resulting right triangle.

content.prompt: Find the value of $\theta$. Answer to 1 decimal place. Draw a perpendicular from the apex to the base. In an isosceles triangle it bisects the base.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle with base 6, right sloping side labelled 10, matching double ticks on both sloping sides and theta at the lower-right vertex. No altitude is included in the question. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: An altitude from the apex bisects the base, giving adjacent side 3 and hypotenuse 10.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated angle or auxiliary construction is supplied.

answer.worked:
Draw a perpendicular from the apex to the base. In an isosceles triangle it bisects the base, so each half is $3$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{3}{10}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{10}\right)\\\theta&\approx72.5^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
